# Octatrack (MKI, MKII): agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-21, research snapshot `ac55c65383b3`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Brief version: rules, recovery, bugs, incidents and open questions. The full pack [octatrack.md](octatrack.md) adds all facts.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]
- **A79** Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01. [hw]
- **A80** A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit. [hw]
- **A81** A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself. [?]
- **A82** On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part. [hw]
- **A83** Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one. [hw]
- **A84** When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too. [hw]
- **A85** A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself. [hw]
- **A86** Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model. [emu] [hw]
- **A87** Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card. [hw]
- **A88** When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects. [hw]
- **A89** On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Octatrack (MKI, MKII)

- **C4** (C) Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour. The earlier digikit README said "no audio"; the current ElekLabs Features that cross the ColdFire-SHARC boundary need both processors emulated together, or a unit: dn2mk2's BOUNCE passed a ColdFire-only gate and failed on units. On the Octatrack the DSP AMP envelope restart only showed as clicks on a unit. Incidents: [I58](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i58-a-wavetable-machine-clicked-on-every-note), [I66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i66-a-feature-that-crosses-coldfire-and-dsp-passed-the-gate-and-failed-on-units). An emulator that plays no samples cannot find the cause of an audible fault: KYOTI's first fix for an Octatrack jump pop, inferred there, changed nothing on the unit, and a render with real audio then showed the hard voice kill ([I119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i119-a-direct-jump-jump-popped-with-silence-tracks-on-the-emulators-inferred-fix-did-not-help)). README has ColdFire + SHARC+ running together with audio, but the DSP "does not run in real time yet", and dn2mk2 reports the emulators do not model the two chips' timing. DSP overruns show up only on a unit. `[doc]` {digikit-old} Incidents: [I36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x). Also [I143](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i143-gearmulators-dsp56300-jit-misexecuted-cmpm-and-xy-half-writes-gearmulator-md-mm).
- **C9** (C) After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). [I73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i73-an-old-project-stopped-all-sound-on-a-sample-machine-mod) (an old project silenced every track), [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (mod data lost at a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT). `[hw]` Also [I154](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i154-a-project-load-dropped-installed-effects-from-the-next-starts-list-modwerk-octatrack-base-up-to-078) (Octatrack: a project load replaced Modwerk's effect map, and installed effects were refused at the next start).
- **C12** (C) Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes} A test failure right after a restart can be stock's boot too: in digikit's emulator the Digitakt II dropped stock MidiRpc requests while its boot intro ran, which failed a storage test (not yet checked on a unit); wait for the firmware's own ready state before the first request ([I114](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i114-stock-midirpc-requests-were-lost-while-the-boot-intro-still-ran)).
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`); on the Octatrack `0x80000012` (MIDI tracks shown) is a long, so a byte read always gives 0 ([I123](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i123-a-byte-read-of-a-long-flag-hid-the-midi-tracks)). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}
- **E3** (E) Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB7** EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming.
- **SB8** About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: finish a completed stage from a 60 Hz tick, or stall EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits.
- **SB9** A Plays-Free MIDI track stalls after its first step (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's BATCH_BUGFIXES (`MIDI_PLAYS_FREE_FIX`); hardware-confirmed 2026-08-28.
- **SB10** A pattern that holds only parameter locks shows as empty (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX`) under [PTN]; under [BANK] a full scan of 256 patterns' locks on every LED refresh starved the CPU. Since 2026-11-20 (318 B version) [BANK] also lights a bank whose pattern holds a trigless lock with a locked value, by reading only the trigless-lock masks and at most 16 lock rows per pattern; confirmed responsive with [BANK] held on an MKI. Other lock-only content still reads empty under [BANK]. {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121}
- **SB11** A pattern-triggered Part change carries the old Part's state over (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`PART_CHANGE_CARRYOVER_FIX`): republish the recorder records, set the voice-kill bit, re-seed the slot.
- **SB12** A trigless lock stays lit after its last lock is erased (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS (a deliberately empty trigless lock placed with FUNC + TRIG is left alone); since 2026-11-20 on MIDI tracks too, confirmed on an MKI (I173).
- **SB13** LO-FI's AMF ring-mod pitch falls at eleven values instead of rising (Octatrack MKI and MKII, OS 1.40C (LO-FI on FX1 and FX2); open in stock; fixed by a mod (not yet run on hardware per the Modwerk draft)). Workaround: `mpyuu` instead (octa-bt-pt's LOFI AMF FIX; also a Modwerk draft module). Saved projects at affected values will sound different with the fix.
- **SB14** Probable: SPATIALIZER's ring misaligns when selected mid-play (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; unconfirmed). Workaround: none yet; the source plans a hardware test on stock.
- **SB17** The AUDIO EDITOR key opens the sample the track had before (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: reselect the track first; fixed by OCTAMAX 2f.
- **SB22** One Part byte outside its stock range drops the whole bank at power-on (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: store only values stock accepts in stock records (rule A60).
- **SB26** Probable: TRACK COPY / PASTE leaves the LFO designer behind (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; unconfirmed). Workaround: none yet; KYOTI names a fix (TRACK_PASTE_DESIGNER_FIX, about 60-100 bytes) if it is confirmed.
- **SB29** WAV files saved by the Octatrack carry a RIFF size 8 bytes too large (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; confirmed in emulator, not checked on a unit-saved file). Workaround: tools that read Octatrack WAVs should trust the `data` chunk size.
- **SB30** FX1 SETUP knob F on EQUALIZER changes a hidden Part byte (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; unconfirmed on a unit; audible effect unknown). Workaround: leave knob F alone on that page.
- **SB32** A timestretched voice retriggered within about 300 samples stays silent (Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour (a limit more than a bug)). Workaround: keep slices and retrigger gaps above ~300 samples, or turn timestretch off for them; octabam's LAZY CHOP guards against it.
- **SB33** Deleting an arrangement row above a JUMP that targets it turns the JUMP into a HALT (Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour, reproduced on the developer's MKI with no module). Workaround: check JUMP targets after deleting rows.
- **SB34** Inserting on a HALT row leaves an endless LOOP below it (Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: check the rows after an insert near a HALT.

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I5** EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (stock USB driver). Cause: stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head. Fix: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming. Rules: A39.
- **I6** About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered. Cause: the stage completes inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stops part-way. Fix: a 60 Hz tick finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. Rules: A39.
- **I7** A soft reset leaves the USB controller running. Cause: the controller and PHY keep their state over a soft reset. Fix: stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0), wait ~50 ms, then reset; 20 of 20 good boots. Rules: A40.
- **I28** A select value outside its count stalled the sequencer. Cause: stored values no longer fit the new layout. Fix: stamp old projects' stored values after a layout change. Rules: E3,C9.
- **I29** DSP scratch at `$84` and up hung the unit. Cause: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block; above it belongs to others. Fix: stay inside the per-instance block. Rules: D11.
- **I30** Key events posted into stock's queues crashed the unit minutes later. Cause: events posted straight into stock's internal queues. Fix: feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. Rules: A50.
- **I31** Restoring DSP-read state every frame corrupted the audio. Cause: a mod overwrote data the DSP reads each frame; doing so is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping. Fix: restore only CPU-side state. Rules: A50.
- **I32** A DSP frame counter saturated after 50.7 minutes. Cause: a counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`. Fix: mask counters to 23 bits. Rules: A51.
- **I33** Module state on a load-meter counter gave a jittery pitch. Cause: module state at `X:$2840`, core 1's load-meter counter. Fix: move the state. Rules: D11.
- **I34** A startup change stalled at the logo after a long power-off. Cause: unknown; keeping the activation helper resident fixed it. Fix: qualify startup changes after a long power-off. Rules: A40.
- **I35** USB replies stayed stale for minutes. Cause: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. Fix: copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. Rules: A48,A28.
- **I48** A menu table in a "free" zero run crashed the unit. Cause: the 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` lies in the PROJECT subsystem's RAM (the zero region above `0x400d8000`). Fix: larger code goes to a loader-copied area (octabam's loader stub at `0x4010fdf0`). Rules: D11,A43.
- **I57** A demand-loader soak froze an Octatrack MKII. Cause: the demand loader's BASE/MODULATION transition is the larger factor (only the loader changed between the two images, and the rate fell from about 1 in 6 to 1 in 118); STEM REC and its 18 MiB reserve are not cleared. Candidate for the total freeze: two waits in the frame interrupt with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin until the DSP takes the frame's host command). Fix: partial (one copy per load). Time limits on the waits and copying a slice per frame are proposed, not made. Rules: A51,A29.
- **I58** A wavetable machine clicked on every note. Cause: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START; with any ATK above 0 a sound that keeps playing across trigs drops to silence and fades back in. Fix: hold the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shape AMP in the machine, as SYNTH MACHINE does (W5). Rules: C4.
- **I59** Patch state inside a stock task's buffer silenced tracks. Cause: patch state at `0x80006a00-0x80007000` lay inside the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task (`0x80006964-0x80007574`). The crash is not proven to come from this. Fix: OCTAMAX_2h keeps all patch state in DDR; the build refuses any operand that points into the buffer. Rules: A43,A50.
- **I60** A long copy with interrupts masked clicked on every reload. Cause: a 43 KB pattern copy ran with interrupts masked and held off the audio frame. Fix: copy with interrupts on and publish only the slices that changed. Also fixed in the same round: reloading the current pattern while another was cued let the cued one land anyway. Rules: A34.
- **I69** A mod took stock's USB DISK MODE pause for a DSP stall and kept the audio off. Cause: stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open. The base's stall watch read that pause as a stalled DSP, and its recovery held the audio stopped. It was never reproduced on a stock unit. Fix: the base tells that pause from a stall (2026-11-10); on the owner's MKII the walk, about 10 s in the mode, NO and PLAY now plays. Rules: C12.
- **I72** A drum machine mod played silent hits after power-up and misread stock's voice start. Cause: the hit level was scaled from a base read only when a restore bit at `0x80001538` was clear, and on the unit that bit can be set at power-up, so the base stayed 0. Separately, the mod's wrapper of the FLEX voice start passed two arguments where stock's routine `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` takes three, so stock read a word of the wrapper's stack. Fix: the base is now the lane's VOL; the wrapper forwards all three arguments, and stock's retrigs run. Rules: G8,C10.
- **I75** Removing a synth module that tracks still used left the loader stuck in recovery. Cause: not traced in the source; the module's README now says to remove it only while no track in the Part uses it. Fix: a power cycle brought the unit back. Rules: A54.
- **I78** The first PLAY after power-on started a track's recorder. Cause: a quantized REC start left staged at `0x800018be`/`0x800018de` (the QREC branch of REC_POST `0x40005178`). Whether stock alone does this is unclear. Fix: FREE LOOP's `stray_guard` stops such a recording; not seen on images 42-43. Rules: A40,G8.
- **I79** Three FM Synth tracks beside a busy pattern froze an Octatrack. Cause: the CPU-rendered machines were not counted against any budget, so nothing stopped the load from passing the frame (measured by the fix, not traced further). Fix: the base prices each CPU machine, refuses a pick over the limit (CPU FULL) and drops voices at the frame guard; the same set then played on a development build. A busy project may now drop FM Synth notes. Rules: A25,A34.
- **I82** A frame interrupt entering about 150 µs late stopped an Octatrack's DSP frame exchange. Cause: at START and at a program change one frame interrupt runs 475-585 µs (a frame is 362.8 µs), so the next one enters late. A log of entry times showed: 128-149 µs late, the unit catches up; 155-223 µs late, it skips one frame and runs on; both stalls entered 149 and 155 µs late. A USB capture adds 25-30 µs to the START frame and moved it onto that boundary; adding 60 µs to every frame interrupt without a capture moved it past and caused no stall. Inferred: the ColdFire's transfer chain is still sending when the DSP starts its next frame. Fix: octabam's FRAME GUARD holds an entry 110-190 µs late until it is 190 µs late, so the DSP skips one frame cleanly; with it 32 first STARTs and 192 program changes ran without a stall at 20 channels. A first version mis-reduced the lateness after a skip and still stalled in a long program-change soak; corrected 2026-11-13. Not measured: what the skipped frame does to sounding audio; an MKI. Rules: A56.
- **I83** Reading the CF card from a mod's UI tick froze an Octatrack. Cause: the player read the card from AERIA's UI tick; stock does its card work in its own card task. Fix: v32 switched the player off (plan: read in the card task, or preload the file into RAM); starting the screensaver no longer stalls. Rules: A57.
- **I85** A delay effect left the next effect in its DSP slot silent. Cause: moving PT2399 to another block of core 1's X memory (`X:$2000`) stopped it. Fix: a build that survived 12 rounds of the trigger and 30 random swaps; PT2399 shares memory with BBD, HAIL and AURORA, so those pairs are refused; BBD removed in v0.9.3. Rules: A58.
- **I86** An own engine filled the output half that was about to play: late samples on the analog outputs only. Cause: the engine wrote into the half of its output DMA buffer that was about to play. Fix: the engine fills the other half; noise through the loop then arrived with one delay at all 16 positions. Rules: A58.
- **I95** One byte a mod stored made stock drop a whole Octatrack bank at restart. Cause: VECTOR packed SPAN into a byte's top bits, so SPAN 8-12 stored 0x80 or more; stock's Part check counts that as bad, and at boot the battery restore runs before the base has its modules back, so VECTOR's wrapper around the check did not apply (SB22). Fix: 0.3.2 moves SPAN's top bit to a free bit of the next byte and rewrites old bytes; the bank stayed intact on restart. Rules: A60,E3.
- **I96** Every effect pick was refused with NO ROOM after a restart. Cause: a restore makes all modules live in one pass and the board binds Sidechain's key-bus slot on a later tick, so Air Chorus's buffer took the block before the key bus was counted and every later pick failed. Fix: the base counts live controllers that no slot holds yet; host-tested only. Rules: G8.
- **I105** Module picks accepted while stopped stalled the DSP once the unit played. Cause: the busy-unit guard judged the stopped load, which is 15-25 points below the playing load, and did not count the picked machine's own cost. Fix: the guard now adds the machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load ("WAS BUSY PLAYING"). Rules: A65.
- **I107** An Octatrack left USB during a USB Audio recording on a module trial. Cause: unknown (the module, the recording or the development base); six recordings on 2026-11-14 ended normally. Fix: none yet. Rules: C11.
- **I108** A demand load during play stalled an Octatrack's DSP until the copy moved to the frame's end. Cause: DSP core B reached P:`$268` in its first track and stopped, and core A waited at P:`$a3` for good. Frame overrun, the copy alone, its destination, the stack and a stale X word were ruled out; the mechanism is unknown (the emulator port runs one core and cannot show it). Fix: the loader's copy (DLCOPY) moved from the frame head (P:`0x76`) to the frame end (P:`0x342`); 12 of 12 runs with 251 loads were clean on 2026-11-15. Rules: A66,A56.
- **I109** A module restarted an Octatrack with an illegal instruction its cache still held. Cause: the code was present in the cache but read as zeros through the uncached alias. The same package on a twin without the base change ran clean, so the base change is suspected. Fix: none yet; Amiga 0.3.0's later RAM trial rolled back clean. Rules: C11.
- **I110** A remote-commanded REMIX SWITCH boot stopped on the boot screen. Cause: it was the first boot after flashing, after a project load, panel PLAY, MIDI START, two program changes, STOP and commands 1, 2 and 4. The next nine commanded boots all came back in 7-8 s, two of them after the same sequence. Fix: none; seen once. Rules: A2,A40.
- **I118** Card-loaded mods copied stock bytes the flashed build had already patched (Digitone mk1, Octatrack). Cause: a loader that fills a mod's replayed stock instructions from the running OS reads the flashed core's or companions' patches instead; the OS also changes some image data before the load point (1,238 bytes on the Digitone from `0x4018fefc`; Octatrack data in `0x400b9000..0x400e2324`). Fix: the build descriptor carries a stock shadow of every range the flashed build writes (ABI 1.2), and the core keeps a copy of the OS image made before the OS runs. Rules: A69.
- **I119** A DIRECT JUMP jump popped with SILENCE TRACKS on; the emulator's inferred fix did not help. Cause: at a switch the engine hard-kills each silenced voice (`0x40006820`), with no declicked release. Stock's change lands on step 0, where most tracks trigger and restart in the same frame; the jump lands mid-pattern, so a ringing track with no trig there is simply cut. Fix: V7.2.2 calls stock's note-off `0x40008f84(t)` for every track the switch will silence, about a tick before it (the DSP's own fade). The author: "the pattern change pop seems to be fixed" (2026-11-15). Rules: C4,A58.
- **I121** Hiding a window by unlinking it let stock build SETUP inside it. Cause: Clyps hid its window by unlinking it; the window manager `0x4005829c` finds a free slot by the linked bit (`+32` bit 5), so a SETUP window opened during the peek was built into Clyps' own slot. A plain press of the current page also reached stock, which toggles SETUP. The UI gate missed it: its screen shots were stock's page layer only, never the composed screen. Fix: CL36 hides the window by its visible bit (`+32` bit 0) and brings it to the front (`0x400117b4`) on return; CL37/CL38 also hide the SETUP window's edges and re-push Clyps' key layers after a peek. The gate now compares the screen as composed (`0x40013abc` into `[0x400b9710]`). Passed on the unit in KYOTI V1.8C (2026-11-15). Rules: A50.
- **I122** Redirecting one stock painter drew half track tabs and a stray mark. Cause: three routines paint each tab, each with its own active-track test (`0x4004bd48` lower half, `0x4003fed8` upper half, `0x40044804` status mark); the first probe had listed the other writers too, but only one was redirected. Renders that called a painter alone did not show the mark. Fix: all three tests redirected (CLYPX, all good on the unit the same day); renders now call the whole per-pass routine `0x40052200`. Rules: A31.
- **I123** A byte read of a long flag hid the MIDI tracks. Cause: the "MIDI tracks shown" flag `0x80000012` is a long; a byte read returns its high byte, always 0. The emulator gate passed because its fixture project loaded with the audio tracks shown. RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT's `rl3_arm_n` has the same byte read (reported, status not stated). Fix: read as a long (CLYP7); a gate scenario on a project that loads with the MIDI tracks shown. Rules: D13.
- **I124** A flashed image carried another build's OS VERSION name. Cause: a later composite build re-ran the base builder without a name and rewrote the same output file; the code (mainos) was the intended one, the name and the reported syx hashes were not. The card `.bin` is ELUP-obfuscated, so the name cannot be read there. Fix: build the composite without rebuilding the base, and check the "OS VERSION will read" line and the syx hash against a fresh named build before reporting. Rules: A6.
- **I129** An Octatrack restore left out the same module at nearly every start. Cause: a set the unit accepts at a sync does not always fit again at the restore; not reproduced. Fix: none yet; Modwerk plans to restore that set in the emulator. Rules: C11.
- **I130** A timed module trial could not roll back while the module's window was open. Cause: base 0.7.5 refuses to remove, replace or undo a module while stock's window manager or input layer still names its memory (`RUNTIME_UI_OPEN`); the timed trial's rollback had no path for it. Fix: after NO closed the window, `device -- recover` rolled the trial back; a second trial with the window closed rolled back at once. The site's handling of a trial that ends with a window open is not yet tested. Rules: A54,A2.
- **I146** PATTERN MUTE stored its layer in the one-shot trig mask (octabam). Cause: the module used bits 0-1 of byte 40 of each audio track record, which is the low byte of the one-shot trig mask (steps 1-8). The check that called the byte unused ran on a project with no one-shots on steps 1-2. The switch counted any two FUNC presses, chords included. Fix: PATTERN-layer mutes moved to a side file `pmute.work` (STORE client 11, 512 B, CRC-32) plus a 48-byte battery copy at `0x100fbdc0`; projects saved under 0.4 load no PATTERN mutes and keep their one-shots; a pattern copy no longer carries PATTERN mutes. The switch now drops a pending FUNC press once the panel row states show another key. The gate now seeds one-shots on steps 1-2. Rules: A43,A77.
- **I154** A project load dropped installed effects from the next start's list (Modwerk Octatrack base up to 0.7.8). Cause: a project load replaced the base's effect map; a module that stayed on its handle was left unnamed, so the save dropped its line. Found from the diagnostics and reproduced in a host test. Fix: base 0.7.9 names every module that stays on its handle and gives legacy projects the catalogue's handle. Rules: C9.
- **I155** Arr Rows drew its selection wrong and pasted as an insert (Modwerk draft, Octatrack MKI). Cause: the module read `0x460d16e8` as the first row shown (stock's is `0x460d1c64`), and judged CUE from its own key count, which a missed release left stuck. Found on the unit, diagnosed in the emulator. The MIDI stop is unexplained. An earlier build had marked the bank bit `0x100b14ce` instead of the arrangement bit `0x100b14d1`; the emulator caught that, the host test could not. Fix: the stock row variable, and CUE state read from stock. Rules: A50.
- **I158** A mis-encoded DSP multiply put garbage on the Octatrack's headphones (AERIA OS). Cause: a multiply in the DSP engine had its operands in an order the assembler silently encodes as the signed-by-unsigned `mpysu`, so the sample was read as unsigned. Fix: operands reordered (builds of 2026-11-15, tested and flashed on the unit); the build script now refuses a DSP listing with an `mpysu`-encoded multiply or with unassembled lines. Rules: A41.
- **I159** Headphones silent after flashing, though every RAM-boot bench test passed (AERIA OS). Cause: at a cold start core 0 started the ESAI and lined its output rings up with the converter before core 1 set the shared PLL; the PLL lock then stalled it, and the eight output words could sit shifted in the converter's slots (a shift of two puts main on the main jacks and unused words on the headphones). A RAM boot runs with the PLL already locked, so no bench test could see it. Also found: AERIA's MKII headphone left and right were swapped against stock. Fix: v0.9.5-beta (2026-11-19): the engine waits for a host flag raised 20 ms after core 1 and the PLL are set; the MKII phones order follows stock (right in word 4). Simulator-tested only; the simulator does not model the cold-start clock. The owner's check: cold power-on, sound on main and headphones; if still silent, listen on CUE (main there means the slots are still shifted). Rules: A40.
- **I163** An Octatrack froze while playing after the walk PROJ, DOWN, YES, YES (Modwerk base 0.7.9). Cause: unknown. Freezes while stopped after this walk were read earlier as OS upgrades or USB DISK MODE seen by the freeze watch, but this one was playing and kept its base. Fix: none yet. Modwerk's test: on 0.7.9 with that set, play, repeat the walk and read the log. Rules: A29.
- **I164** A 303 voice lost its last step, popped and played a blip at Part and pattern changes (KYOTI BLACKPYRAMIDS_303). Cause: the voice asked the UI Part, which stock moves about 7 ticks before the switch, so the outgoing track changed a step early; a note's gate was worked out a step ahead from its own pattern only; and GATE was read from the live SETUP byte, which stock re-stages only at the track's trig (0 after a load). Fix: read stock's per-track Part pair, re-time a tied note from the next pattern's first steps, and read GATE from the scheduled pattern's Part. OCTABAM43 passed all checks; the same code is in KYOTI V1.8BC FINAL (2026-11-19). All three bugs were in the earlier FINAL too. Rules: A82,A79.
- **I165** A FLEX SRC page pasted onto a 303 track left a 303 with FLEX's numbers (KYOTI V1.8BC). Cause: the 303 machine is stored as FLEX in the machine bytes plus a signature in NEIGHBOR's bytes; a page paste writes one machine's twelve bytes and the machine byte, never the signature. Fix: hooks at the page copy core, the page paste and the page UNDO set the machine before stock writes. The rebuilt image behaved as intended on the unit, 2026-11-19. Rules: A77.
- **I166** The sequencer stayed on step 1 after a 303 track was pasted into another Part's pattern (KYOTI V1.8BC, seen once). Cause: unknown; the author could not repeat it, and an ot_emu replay of the steps ran normally in every variant. Fix: none; if it comes back, record the steps and build a diagnostic image. Rules: A29.
- **I167** Holding a step again deleted its trig (octabam LOCK EDIT). Cause: LOCK EDIT's hold hook kept the lock popup closed but returned before stock's hold handler cleared the key's hold bit; the release toggles the trig while that bit is set. Fix: the hook clears the bit itself and still keeps the popup closed; a gate holds again for 400 ms and checks that the step survives. Rules: A50.
- **I168** Per-track trig modes were saved but gone after a power cycle (TRACK TRIG MODE). Cause: a power-up restores the project from battery RAM and never parses `project.work`, and the mode table was in DRAM. The QUICK MUTE exit treated the passing mode as a pick. Fix: the table moved to 8 bytes of battery RAM; a step out of TRACKS, QUICK MUTE or DELAY CONTROL never overwrites a track's mode. ACCLOOP15 passed switching, save, reload and a power cycle on the MKI. Rules: A40.
- **I169** A project reload after a demand-loader phase left the DSP frame count stopped (octabam BUILD 05). Cause: unknown. Fix: none; workaround: boot the image again (REMOTE command 3) after each loader phase, which restarted the count without a power cycle. Rules: A51.
- **I170** DARK REV picked on all eight tracks while MODULATION was loaded stopped the DSP (octabam BUILD 05). Cause: it needs MODULATION loaded by the demand loader and live on FX2 when DARK REV, whose buffer reaches the demand effect's code, is picked on every track and START follows. An earlier overwrite of the frame guard's cells is not the cause. Fix: none Rules: A56,A51.
- **I172** A 303 chosen on a FLEX track was silent until switched away and back (KYOTI V1.8BC RC1). Cause: the 303 is stored as FLEX, so FLEX to BLKPYRAMD is FLEX to FLEX for stock, and stock's machine commit re-stages a track's live machine bytes only for PICKUP; otherwise they follow at the track's next trig after a real machine change, or at a Part apply. The voice played FLEX's live values (VOL = FLEX's TSTR byte: OFF gives silence). The project's checks seeded the bytes before PLAY, so none caught it. The same was in V1.8BC FINAL. Fix: after a machine commit on the current Part, call stock's seed when the stored machine is FLEX and set the track's Part pair to `0xff`, but not while the track still carries the old Part's note. `KY18BC RC2` passed every item on the unit, 2026-11-20. Rules: A85.
- **I173** A fix for erased trigless locks covered audio tracks only (KYOTI ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS). Cause: the LIVE erase calls a separate MIDI twin of the audio worker; the fix had only hooked the audio one. The emulator showed the bug on the FINAL and RC1 images once a MIDI case was added. Fix: one shared rule behind two hooks, one per worker (240 B). `KY18BC RC2` passed every MIDI and audio item on the unit, 2026-11-20; promoted the same day. Rules: A84.
- **I174** A track that stopped being a 303 played a burst of its FLEX sample (KYOTI V1.8BC RC2). Cause: the 303 rides on a hidden stock FLEX voice. After the switch the frame's renderer for the track stays the 303's until the track's next trig, and it handed the hidden voice to stock's sample renderer, which played it for about 300 ms. Present since V1.8BC FINAL. Fix: while a track that was a 303 waits for its trig (also when it yields at a cued Part switch), render stock's idle record instead. RC3 carries it. Rules: A85.
- **I175** QUAN read 5/4 instead of 1/1 on entering VARI; VARISPEED and the 303 shared spare bytes (KYOTI VARISPEED). Cause: which meaning a parked byte had (PTCH or QUAN) lived only in RAM and was forgotten at every Part apply, so the next poll read the PTCH park as QUAN (PTCH +12 = `5/4`), and that value was then saved with the Part. Present in every FINAL VARISPEED, VARISPEED_EMUS and KYOTI. A follow-up probe found that VARISPEED parked PTCH in NEIGHBOR's spare bytes, which BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 also used: PTCH was lost or changed, a track that had been a 303 entered VARI at `5/4`, and a real 303's signature could break. A flag in bit 7 was also zeroed by stock's Part validator on every load. Fix: VRG3 keeps VARISPEED's state in four Part bytes nobody else uses, each below 128, with the meaning in the bytes; older projects are migrated at first sight, and VARISPEED never touches a 303 track. Confirmed on the unit in RC1 (VARI entry, QUAN across a save, a project from the old build, a 303 beside VARI), 2026-11-20; promoted. Rules: A77,A60.
- **I176** A USB Audio Undo froze the panel and left the Octatrack off USB (Modwerk 0.7.11 candidates). Cause: (1) after a descriptor change only the UI tick could switch the USB controller back on (host test); (2) not proven: the base started its host deadline when it set the controller's run bit and never checked that the controller attached. Fix: a one-second fallback in the frame interrupt re-enables the controller; later the base checks attach, suspend and reset after three seconds and offers the descriptors once more if VBUS is valid and the port stayed disconnected. Release base 0.7.12 then passed eight trials (2 to 20 channels, Track 8/Master twice), Keep, a power cycle and a restore from the card. Rules: A88,A55.
- **I177** A paired browser tab rolled back USB Audio trials at the reconnect (Modwerk). Cause: the macOS USB log showed the browser opening the vendor interface about 200 ms before the test tool; the site's link undoes an unfinished trial when a paired page reconnects. The log does not show an Undo command from the browser. Fix: with the browser closed, Main + Cue passed three times in a row and all six layouts recorded; Modwerk's guide says to close paired tabs before a native USB Audio trial, and the site now leaves another session's USB Audio trial running when the unit reconnects. Rules: A88.
- **I178** Analog BD stayed silent after a rolled-back trial until a power cycle (Modwerk base 0.7.9). Cause: the base released the module's DSP engine for good while the trial was still open. Fix: base 0.7.10 keeps the module ready to come back until the trial is kept or rolled back, while still giving its DSP room to the trial. Release candidate on an MKII: the kick measured -19.3 dBFS on T4 before and after a 60 s trial that removed Analog BD and added Vibrato. Rules: A54.
- **I179** A VECTOR trial's Undo left the loader in recovery until a power cycle (Modwerk 0.7.11 development image). Cause: before removing a departing track machine the loader checked its stock menu definitions as they read with the machine still patched in, so it saw the machine as still in use. The log did not name the reference that blocked. Fix: the loader now judges a departing machine's menu entries as they will read after its stock handlers return, and still checks cached callbacks and every Part live. Five later VECTOR trials (stopped and after playback, three builds, the release candidate included) rolled back normally. Rules: A54.
- **I180** A project load after a card restore stalled the DSP (Modwerk 0.7.9 development base). Cause: the base's DSP manager began changing which effects the DSP held while the bank and Parts were still loading: at the stall core 0 had bound SPATIALIZER and the manager waited for core 1's SPRING REV bind, with the incoming effect map not yet published. Why the frame edge went missing is open. Fix: a gate that continues open requests but starts no new plan until the whole effect map is loaded (base 0.7.11). On 0.7.11 two restoring boots loaded with no extra DSP packet or commit; shipped 0.7.10 did not stall in two tries either but made the same residency changes the stall trace had shown. Rules: A89,A56.
- **I84** Uninitialised shared-window memory crashed DSP core 1 on a cold boot; the emulator starts it at zero. Cause: core 1's slot table in the shared window held random values at power-on; the emulator zeroes that memory. Fix: core 1 clears its table before it starts. Rules: C10.
- **I117** Two ColdFire instruction forms where GCC and ot_emu disagree (Octatrack, emulator). Cause: for `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` GCC assumes the destination uses the old a0 and ot_emu the new one; for a byte push to `-(sp)` GCC assumes SP moves by 1 and ot_emu by 2. Fix: `dl_memcpy` kept out of line and `-fno-ipa-sra`, so neither form is in the build. Rules: A42.
- **I120** A landing on the boundary tick was exact in the emulator and sometimes a step off on the unit. Cause: CL25 landed on the boundary tick and purged the old boundary event only if its fire time was at or after the sample clock; on the unit that clock runs in audio frames, so the comparison flipped by a frame and the old step stayed. Tick-level oracles in the emulator had passed. Fix: CL26 lands a tick before the boundary (ahead 2) and purges a full tick ahead (measured margin: one tick in every purge); RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT and DIRECT JUMP V7.1 took the same rule. CL29 "timing correct" on the unit. Rules: A70.
- **I76** A loader base update over USB said Done but did not stick. Cause: unknown. Fix: update again and check the base version after the reboot. Rules: A23.
- **I100** A Windows PC could not open the Octatrack's vendor interface. Cause: Windows writes that value only at an interface's first setup; why it was missing on members' PCs is unknown. Fix: the base reports `bcdDevice` 0x0101, which made Windows write the value again. Rules: A63.
- **I148** OS UPGRADE from the card installed an older base .bin (Modwerk). Cause: stock's choice between several `.bin` files at the card's top level; the rule is unknown. Fix: the guide says to remove every other `.bin` and to rerun if the old base comes back. Rules: A6.
- **I149** A trial rollback timed out halfway and left the unit in recovery (Modwerk). Cause: the base undoes a set one module at a time; 24 modules need more than 3 s. Fix: the tool waits up to 20 s. Rules: A54.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O22** Has octabam's WAVE (wavecf) run on an Octatrack?: A) module README: "Not flashed" B) CHANGELOG: unit builds W1-W6 on 2026-11-07, clicks gone from W5 (I58)
- **O23** Octatrack boot fill of internal SRAM; meaning of `0x80000003`: A) KYOTI NOTES: 0x3e88 bytes copied and the rest zero-filled up to `0x80004000`; the playing pattern's Part is the slab link, and `0x80000003` "is not it" B) OCTAMAX NOTES: `.data`/`.bss` up to `0x80008000`, filled from the image tail; `0x80000003` is the active Part (verified on a unit)
- **O30** Octatrack PLAYING byte: A) octabam EVENTS.md and the REMOTE README: `0x800065b8`, with its writers `0x4009c3d4` / `0x4009c4d4` B) octabam HARDWARE_TESTING.md: `wait_stopped` polls `0x800065bb` until it leaves 1
- **O31** Lowest safe word for code in the Octatrack DSP window: A) devices/octatrack.md (octabam port): resident window code is safe from `0x33da3`, DARK REV writes up to `0x33da2` `[emu]` B) elekloader dspload-ot 0.2 README: true only with default knobs; a reverb set past its defaults may write further into the window, so dspload-ot adds a guard word at each end of every block {elekloader-1117}
- **O32** Octatrack track record: where the trigless-trig mask sits: A) octatrack.md (octabam REMOTE, {octabam-1116}): trig mask `+0x00..0x07`, trigless mask `+0x10..0x17` B) KYOTI CLYPS_SCOPE §1.18 / §3.5: trigless (lock) trigs at `+0x08`; stock's pattern classifier `0x4009a464` skips `+0x10..0x17`; `+0x08..0x37` hold the trigless and recorder layers {kyoti-clyps-scope}
- **O38** Octatrack DSP cycles per move (probe readings): A) octatrack.md: `move x0,a` 2 cycles, one-word displaced ~4, two-word ~6 `[hw]` B) octabam CHIP.md (2026-11-18, marked unsure): each reading is exactly twice the DSP56300 manual's figure (1, 1, 2, 3); the probe's timer may count at half the clock, and the manual's figures fit MODULATION's unit costs {octabam-1119}
- **O44** Octatrack codec set-up over SPI: A) octatrack.md: stock does not set up the codec over SPI; its only SPI traffic is the real-time clock `[emu]` (octabam emulator trace) {aeria-log} B) AERIA's specification: the bootstrap writes the CS42432's register 07 := FF (all DACs muted) at every boot and the OS must write 07 := 00 (register read by the owner, 2026-11-10) {aeria-1120}
- **O45** Has octabam's form of PAGE LOOP, TRIG MUTE and TRACK TRIG MODE run on an Octatrack?: A) octabam README module table and usage pages: emulator only ("no hardware result is claimed here") B) each module README: ran on an Octatrack MKI since ACCLOOP6 / 15 / 16 (2026-10-25..28); our ot-mods-hteah entry says `tested: unit` {octabam-1120}

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H31** (stock) Stock TRACK COPY / PASTE on the Octatrack does not carry the LFO designer (SB26). Test: On T1 set an LFO WAVE to the designer, draw an obvious shape, aim it at volume with high depth; give T2 a different designer; GRID REC copy T1, paste onto T2: does T2 follow T1's shape?
- **H32** (stock) With SILENCE TRACKS on, stock also pops at a Part-changing pattern change when a ringing track has no trig on the new pattern's step 0 (the hard kill `0x40006820`; I119). Test: OT DEMO, SILENCE TRACKS on: let a sample ring on T4, T5 or T7, change A05 -> A03 with CHAIN AFTER 2; listen for a pop; repeat with SILENCE TRACKS off.
- **H33** (stock) The brief "new settings on the old sound" heard at a FULL load (Clyps) is stock's single sound path per track, not the mod: a retriggered voice fades through a path that already carries the new Part. Test: Stock [PTN] + trig between two patterns on different Parts with clearly different settings on one track and a sample ringing up to the change; the same blip on stock settles it.
- **H40** (stock) Octatrack stock LFO-design Invert maps v to -1 - v and Clear sets all steps to 0 and stepped. Test: Invert and clear a custom LFO on the unit, save, and read the Part's 16 values and interpolation mask.
- **H50** (stock) A `.wav` saved by a stock Octatrack holds the file size, not size - 8, in its RIFF header (bytes 4-7). Test: Save any sample or recorder buffer on a unit; read bytes 4-7 as little endian and compare with the file size.
- **H51** (stock) With several .bin files at the CF card's top level, Octatrack OS UPGRADE picks one by a fixed rule (name order or file date), not the newest. Test: Put two copies of the stock 1.40C .bin with different names and dates on the card (both stock, so nothing changes), run OS UPGRADE and note which file it names or reads; swap names and repeat.
- **H58** (stock) Stock Octatrack OS 1.40C reads a trig condition above 64 (octabam's TRIG MUTE stores condition + 65) as no condition: it plays the trig, shows ERR, and the bank still loads (no BANK UNAVAILABLE, cf. A60). Test: Load a project saved with a TRIG MUTE build on stock 1.40C (back up first): does the muted trig play, does its condition read ERR, does the bank load?
- **H59** (stock) A stock Octatrack power-up never parses `project.work`; it restores the project from battery RAM (I168). Test: With the unit off, edit the tempo in `project.work` on the card (keep a copy), power on: the old tempo should stay until LOAD PROJECT.
- **H21** (build) The Octatrack stall after a PROJECT > SYSTEM walk on Modwerk builds is Modwerk's DSP stall watchdog firing while stock itself holds the frames (USB DISK MODE), not a stock fault. Test: Make the same walk on a unit with nothing installed, then with the watchdog off.
- **H22** (build) The total freeze in octabam's demand-loader soak (I57) is the ColdFire spinning in one of the frame interrupt's waits that have no time limit, after the DSP stopped taking host words. Test: Add time limits (with a counter) to both waits and repeat the 118-switch soak.
- **H29** (build) On the Octatrack's ColdFire (MCF5445x), a byte push to `-(sp)` moves SP by 2 and `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` uses the incremented a0, as ot_emu models it (GCC assumes otherwise; I117). Test: Run a tiny probe that executes both forms and logs SP and the written address to the card or a battery-RAM word.
- **H30** (build) The Octatrack comes back up normally from a ColdFire soft reset (RCR `0xFC0A0000` = `0x80`) started on the engine task; stock never restarts itself. Test: Trigger the reset from a minimal mod on a unit with a known recovery path; check boot, card mount and project load.
- **H35** (build) Clocking an Octatrack on a USB-MIDI mod base (Modwerk, octabam) from USB and DIN at once doubles the tempo and saves it into the project, because the base passes every USB clock tick to stock's clock handler without checking for DIN clock. Test: Send 120 BPM clock on DIN and USB together for 30 s; read the tempo, then reload the project.
- **H67** (build) On stock Octatrack OS 1.40C, erasing a MIDI trigless lock's trigs in LIVE REC ([NO] + [TRACK] while the playhead passes) leaves the step's trigless-lock flag (`+0x10`) set over an empty lock row, and the trig row keeps showing a trigless lock there, while the same gesture on an audio track clears it. Test: On a stock unit, place a MIDI trigless lock with a locked CC, erase it with [NO] + [TRACK] in LIVE REC and look at the step in GRID REC; repeat on an audio track.
- **H65** (build) Binding a DSP module at about 95 % CPU stalls the Octatrack's DSP frame exchange: four field stalls on Modwerk bases before 0.7.9 had the manager binding, core 0's last packet a BIND, every earlier frame on time. Test: On base 0.7.9 or later, bind a module at about 95 % CPU and read the stall record; the emulator cannot show it (it never places DSP code).

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).
